{{Top|ga|leg}}
{{Quote|Winter is when the boars can't get out and fight one another either, so they get all cozy and pleasant&mdash;they really do&mdash;and write songs and poems to their sows. Or, they hire me to write songs and poems.|Sebastin Onyx|<ref name="Murder">{{JournalCite|14|Murder in Slushtime}}</ref>}}
'''Gamorrean poetry''' was written in the [[Gamorrese]] [[Language/Legends|language]] by and for members of the [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. Gamorrean [[Gender/Legends|males]] would write [[Poet/Legends|poetry]] for their [[Marriage/Legends|wives]] during [[Winter/Legends|winter]], or for females they intended to court. Some Gamorreans hired [[Author/Legends|ghost-writers]] to write their poems for them, such as [[Liegeus Vorn]] and [[Sebastin Onyx]].

==Description==
[[File:Gamorrean_Runes.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Gamorrean poetry could be written in runes.]]
Gamorrean poetry was a form of [[Poet/Legends|poetry]]<ref name="Lords">''[[Lords of Nal Hutta]]''</ref> written by or for members of the [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] [[Species/Legends|species]] in the [[Gamorrese]] [[Language/Legends|language]]. It could be written in runes. During [[Winter/Legends|winters]] on the Gamorrean [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], [[Gamorr/Legends|Gamorr]], Gamorrean [[Gender/Legends|males]], called boars, wrote love poems for their [[Marriage/Legends|wives]], called sows.<ref name="Murder" /> They also used poetry when courting during that season. Some Gamorreans would hire [[Author/Legends|ghost-writers]] and pass off their poetry as their own.<ref name="POT">''[[Planet of Twilight]]''</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|Beldorion has drafted me into editing and retaping his formidable library of Huttese pornography. Even my stint on Gamorr, ghost-writing love poems for the boars to pass off as their own when they go courting in the wintertime, wasn’t so fearful.|Liegeus Vorn, to Leia Organa Solo|<ref name="POT" />}}
At the [[Mirrsteel Heights]] towers on the [[Kwenn Space Station/Legends|Kwenn Space Station]] in [[Hutt Space/Legends|Hutt Space]], several [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]-style [[Gorg/Legends|chuba]] [[Cantina/Legends|cantinas]] hosted [[Standard day/Legends|nightly]] readings of Gamorrean poetry.<ref name="Lords" /> At some point, the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Liegeus Vorn]] spent a stint on Gamorr working as a ghost-writer for boars during their courting season.<ref name="POT" /> The Human [[Sebastin Onyx]] also made ends meet by working as a poet for the mostly illiterate boars, which included [[Guth]], who wanted love poems for [[Kufbrug]], a married [[Matron/Legends|Clan Matron]].<ref name="Murder" />

[[File:GamorreanBoarAndSow-EGPM.jpg|thumb|left|250px|A Gamorrean boar (left) and a sow. Some boars wrote love poems for their sows.]]
In [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]],<ref name="Readers">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' places the events of "[[Murder in Slushtime]]" in [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]].</ref> [[Rog]], Kufbrug's son-in-law, purchased a poem written in Gamorrean runes on parchment from Onyx, claiming it was for Guth. In reality, the poem was given to [[Vrokk]], Kufbrug's husband, who was [[Death/Legends|killed]] by a [[kheilwar]] wasp hidden inside the parchment, implicating Guth in the murder. The former [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Callista Ming]], a shipmate of Guth's, conducted an investigation and learned of Gamorrean love poetry from Onyx in the process.<ref name="Murder" /> 

By that [[Standard year/Legends|year]],<ref name="Readers 2">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' places the events of ''[[Planet of Twilight]]'' in [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]], following "[[Murder in Slushtime]]."</ref> Vorn had wound up on the planet [[Nam Chorios/Legends|Nam Chorios]] as an editor of the Hutt [[Beldorion]]'s [[pornography]] collection. When Vorn met the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[Chief of State (New Republic)/Legends|Chief of State]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa Solo]], he remarked that his previous occupation as a ghost-writer of Gamorrean poetry on Gamorr was not as fearful as his present work. The comment caused Organa Solo to laugh.<ref name="POT" />

==Behind the scenes==
Gamorrean poetry first appeared in the [[1997]] novel ''[[Planet of Twilight]]'' by [[Barbara Hambly]].<ref name="POT" /> It was later identified in the [[2015]] sourcebook ''[[Lords of Nal Hutta]]'', a supplement to [[Fantasy Flight Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: Edge of the Empire]]'' [[roleplaying game]].<ref name="Lords" />
